causal_vocabulary.description: Canonical vocabulary for causal modeling in QIPS evidence synthesis

node_types.exposure: Algorithm choice, parameter setting, or intervention variable
node_types.mediator: Intermediate variable through which exposure affects outcome
node_types.confounder: Causes both exposure and outcome; affects association if not controlled
node_types.effect_modifier: Variable that changes the strength or direction of exposure→outcome
node_types.collider: Caused by both exposure and outcome; conditioning creates bias
node_types.control_variable: Held constant in study design to isolate effect

edge_types.confounds: Hidden cause of both X and Y
edge_types.modifies: Strength of X→Y depends on Z
edge_types.correlated: X and Y associated; direction unknown
edge_types.contradicts: One study says X→Y; another says X↛Y

causal_statuses: reported: Authors explicitly state causal claim
inferred: System extracted from observational data
proposed: Candidate causal relationship from literature consensus
validated: Experimental evidence supports causal direction
disputed: Multiple papers contradict; requires experiment
rejected: Evidence does not support causal claim
evidence_designs: controlled_benchmark: Intervention on algorithm; confounders held constant
quasi_experiment: Observational but with matched groups or instrumental variable
observational_benchmark: No intervention; measures association only

confidence_dimensions.extraction_confidence: How reliably did we extract the claim from text? (high/medium/low)
confidence_dimensions.evidence_confidence: How strong is the empirical support for the association? (high/medium/low)
confidence_dimensions.causal_confidence: How confident are we that X causes Y (not just correlated)? (high/medium/low)
confidence_dimensions.mechanism_confidence: How well understood is the causal pathway? (high/medium/low)
confidence_dimensions.external_validity: How likely does this generalize beyond the study population? (high/medium/low)

estimand.name: Name of causal quantity (e.g., 'average treatment effect')
estimand.comparator: What we're comparing against (e.g., 'GA without mechanism')
confounding_set: Variables that must be adjusted or held constant
effect_modifiers: Variables that change effect size or direction
identification_assumptions: No unmeasured confounding: No hidden cause of both treatment and outcome
Positivity: Both treatment levels are possible for some individuals
No interference: One unit's treatment does not affect another's outcome

mediator_candidates: exploration_rate: proportion of novel search space
effect_modifier_candidates: problem_dimension: effect size may depend on D
function_modality: benefit may be larger on multimodal
population_size: small populations may show different effects

validation_statuses: accepted: Edge passes human review; treat as valid for graph
rejected: Evidence does not support edge; remove from graph
requires_experiment: Plausible but needs empirical validation
disputed: Multiple reviewers disagree; flag for discussion
graph_invariants: Every edge has at least one supporting causal claim
Every accepted edge has a human reviewer and timestamp
Every high-confidence edge cites mechanism or experimental evidence
Contradicting edges are represented with separate entries and status
Time ordering is explicit (e.g., diversity_t → update_t+1)
Feedback loops are labeled as cycles, not assumed acyclic
Generated outputs include input hashes and commit SHAs
